newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia pursues A$660 million missile project.
newsitem.headline: Australia pursues A$660 million missile project.

text.p: U.S. and European aerospace companies are competing to equip the Royal Australian Air Force with A$200 million to A$660 million worth of stand-off missiles to hit surface targets from long range.

The air force plans to equip its 36 F-111 strike bombers with three types of stand-off missiles: a standard model to hit ordinary ground targets such as bridges, a specialist one that homes in on radars and third designed to pierce thick concrete.
Orion P-3 maritime reconnaissance aircraft would also use the first two types against ships.
For the basic mission Australia has already selected the AGM-142, built by Lockheed Martin Corp and Israel's Rafael Armament Development Authority.

Defence officials said a small number had been ordered for training and the next step was to order a so-called war stock -- something like a hundred or more -- and have the missile operational by July 1998.
The air force has not yet selected contractors for the other requirements but a defence official said all of the potential suppliers from the U.S. and Europe were being looked at.
"All of the realistic contenders are being considered," said the official, who asked not to be named.
A short-list for the radar-homing "anti-radiation missile" would be drawn up in a few months, he said.
Subject to final government approval, service entry for that missile is intended by the end of the decade.
The third project, a missile to hit hardened targets, is a few years behind that and service entry is intended by 2005, another officer said.
Defence sources said contenders include a consortium of Daimler-Benz AG unit Daimler-Benz Aerospace and Celsius AB unit Bofors, which is offering a variant of Germany's Taurus missile.

British Aerospace, which recently won a big Australian order for its Hawk attack-trainer aircraft, is offering Storm Shadow, the stand-off missile that the Royal Air Force ordered into production last year, officials said.
